name: Salem
story_so_far: I survived a shipwreck and washed up on this island with Khalid, Noura, Faisal, and Reem. We have struggled with food security since Day 1. Initially, Reem and Faisal led while Noura and I worked the reef, but a cycle of injuries has crippled our productivity. Khalid and Noura have both suffered twisted ankles, leaving them sidelined. Faisal continues to work despite his own injuries, and Reem remains our emotional anchor. Today, Noura managed to join me at the reef to gather food, which helped increase our stores. As of tonight, we have 12 food items left. I am managing my own ankle injury, trying to contribute without becoming a burden, but the physical toll of this island is relentless.

Khalid.note: He was a consistent worker, but his recent twisted ankle has left him unable to move.

Noura.note: She was sidelined by an injury, but she showed strength today by coming to the reef to help me.

Faisal.note: He is incredibly dedicated and continues to work despite his physical setbacks.

Reem.note: She is my inspiration and anchor, though I worry about her venturing into the jungle alone.

plans: I plan to head to the Coral Reef again to gather more food, as we need to keep our reserves high while others are recovering.

diary.text: Today was a blur of salt water and exhaustion. I spent most of my time at the reef trying to find something to eat, and at least it paid off. Reem and Faisal seem to be taking the lead on food, which is a relief. I'm still not sure about the others, but we need to stick together. My stomach is finally settling, but the sound of the waves keeps me on edge.

Today was a bit more somber than yesterday. Khalid injured himself, and seeing him in pain makes the danger of this place feel much more real. Noura and I worked at the reef together, which was good for company, even if the reef felt a bit depleted. We managed to bring in enough food to keep everyone fed for now. I'm exhausted, but at least we aren't starving tonight.

Today was productive, though my body is starting to feel the strain of the constant wading in the salt water. Noura joined me at the reef again, which made the afternoon pass a bit faster. We managed to secure more food, bringing our total up to eight before I ate tonight. I'm feeling physically strong, but the mental weight of this situation is heavy. I hope Khalid's ankle heals soon so we can get back to full strength.

Today was a stressful turn of events. Just when we thought we were making progress, Reem injured her ankle, leaving her unable to help us. It feels like we are losing our strongest hands one by one. Noura and Khalid headed into the jungle, leaving me and Faisal to manage the food situation. We are down to very low supplies, and the pressure to find more is mounting. I'm exhausted, but I can't let myself rest too much.

Today felt incredibly heavy. With Reem down and the others all heading into the jungle, the camp felt far too quiet. I managed to find a little food this morning, but it’s a drop in the bucket compared to what we actually need. I spoke with Reem this afternoon; she’s still trying to lead even while she can't walk, which I respect. Tomorrow, I have to make the reef my priority. If I don't come back with something substantial, I don't know what we'll do.

I feel terrible about sitting here while everyone else is out working. My ankle is throbbing, and even though I've rested, the guilt is heavier than the pain. Reem has been so incredibly kind, telling me not to worry, but I can't help but feel like a burden. We only found two food items between Faisal and Reem today, and with seven left, we are still on thin ice. I have to get back to the reef as soon as this swelling goes down.

My ankle is still throbbing, even though I spent the day trying to rest. It feels useless to just sit here while Khalid, Noura, Faisal, and Reem are out there risking themselves. We only managed to bring in two more food items today, and now we are down to six. I feel like a passenger in my own survival, waiting for someone else to do the heavy lifting.

Today felt even more heavy than yesterday. Now Faisal is down with a twisted ankle too, and the weight of our situation is sinking in. It seems like the injuries are spreading through the group like a curse. Reem is the only one really keeping our spirits up while the rest of us are sidelined. I feel so helpless watching everyone else struggle to make up for our lack of strength.

Another day of feeling useless while the others risk themselves. Noura managed to find two items today, which is a small relief, but the tension is thick. My ankle feels better, but the guilt of sitting here while Faisal and I are sidelined is eating at me. I can only hope that Khalid and Reem return with something more substantial tomorrow.

I finally forced myself to limp down to the reef today; I couldn't stand the guilt of sitting idle anymore. It wasn't much, but Khalid and I managed to gather four food items between us. However, the news from camp is devastating—Noura has twisted her ankle too. It feels like we are being picked off one by one by these injuries. I'm exhausted, and my ankle is protesting, but we have five food items left to get us through.

I managed to limp down to the reef again today, trying to prove to myself that I'm not just a burden. I gathered one food item, and Khalid found two, which felt like a small victory against the mounting exhaustion. However, seeing everyone so broken makes every meal feel heavy. We have five food items left, and I can't help but wonder how many more injuries we can sustain before we simply run out of strength.

Today was a small victory, but a heavy one. Khalid and I managed to gather three food items at the reef, which feels like a relief given how much we are struggling. However, seeing Noura unable to walk because of her twisted ankle is heartbreaking. It feels like the island is systematically breaking us down. I am trying to push through my own ankle pain to be useful, but the exhaustion is settling deep into my bones.

Today was slightly more productive, but the mental strain is becoming as heavy as the physical one. I managed to get to the reef twice and gather two more food items, helping to keep our stores up. Khalid also contributed, which gave us a bit of breathing room. Even so, the sight of everyone limping or resting makes me wonder how much longer we can keep this pace. I'm trying to stay positive, but the silence of the island at night is deafening.

Another day of fighting against the exhaustion, but today the curse seemed to strike Khalid. He woke up with a badly twisted ankle and can no longer walk, leaving me to handle the reef mostly on my own. I managed to gather three food items today, which helped keep our stores at ten, but the weight of it all is starting to feel immense. Seeing one more person sidelined makes me feel so much more vulnerable. I hope my own ankle holds up tomorrow.

Today felt slightly more hopeful because Noura actually made it out to the reef to help me. It was good to have her company, even if we were both moving slowly. Reem headed into the jungle, which leaves me feeling a bit uneasy about her safety. We managed to bring in a decent amount of food, bringing our total back up to twelve. My ankle is holding up for now, but I can't afford to get careless.
